author: evgenigordeev
body:
Fixes #740. Codependent with https://github.com/aws/karpenter-provider-aws/pull/9158

## Rollout Restart Drain Strategy

An opt-in drain mode for single-replica workloads (deploys and statefulsets). Instead of evicting the only pod and taking downtime, Karpenter asks the owner to roll itself - a fresh pod comes up first, then the old one goes away.

- **Singleton deploys**: zero downtime - maxSurge brings the new pod up before the old one is deleted.
- **Singleton statefulsets**: brief downtime (no surge), but the drain bypasses blocking PDBs that would otherwise stall it.
- **Multi-replica workloads**: unchanged - still drain via eviction.

Turn it on with the `RolloutRestartDrainStrategy` feature gate (off by default).

### How it decides when to patch

We only trigger a rollout when the owner's `Status` says the previous one is done - same predicate `kubectl rollout status` uses. If a rollout is still in flight, we skip and emit a `RolloutRestartInProgress` event so you can see why the drain is waiting.

For deploys the predicate is:

```go
dep.Generation > dep.Status.ObservedGeneration ||
    dep.Status.UpdatedReplicas < *dep.Spec.Replicas ||
    dep.Status.Replicas > dep.Status.UpdatedReplicas ||       // surge cleanup still in flight
    dep.Status.AvailableReplicas < dep.Status.UpdatedReplicas
```

The `Replicas > UpdatedReplicas` term is the load-bearing one for singletons: once the new surge pod becomes Ready, `UpdatedReplicas == Spec.Replicas == 1` already, but the old pod hasn't been deleted yet - without this term we'd re-patch and clobber the rollout.

The first cut used a 2-minute timestamp dedup, which matched Karpenter's consolidation cadence and basically never fired. Slow-booting pods (~2+ min) got killed every cycle and never reached Ready. The status-based gate fixes that loop.

### Testing

- 8 unit tests in `pkg/controllers/node/termination/terminator/suite_test.go` - feature gate off/on, singleton vs multi-replica, deploys and statefulsets, plus three in-flight-rollout regression cases. `make presubmit` passes.
- Live cluster test with `egordeev/karpenter-controller-aws:1.12.1-rollout-restart2`:
  - Singleton deploy with blocking PDB (`minAvailable: 1`) → drained with zero downtime, PDB bypassed.
  - Singleton statefulset → drained with brief downtime, as expected.
  - Multi-replica deploy and statefulset → still evicted, unchanged.

## Summary

Demotes `RlsTransactionInterceptor` from "primary integration" to "one of three recipe-level strategies." The interceptor still ships and works — existing consumers don't need to change anything — but the docs no longer position it as the recommended default.

Bundled with a small fix: the docs sidebar version was hardcoded as `v0.2.0-alpha` and had drifted four releases without anyone updating it. Now sourced from `package.json`.

## Theme 9D — Why demote

The interceptor:
1. Wraps every authenticated request (including read-only routes) in a Postgres transaction.
2. Holds a pooled connection for the request's lifetime.
3. Is short enough (~30 lines of meaningful logic) that most of the value is in the *explanation* — `set_config` vs `SET LOCAL`, the fail-closed default of `current_setting(..., true)` — not the importable class.

For high-RPS workloads point 2 is meaningful pool pressure. Different apps want different strategies; the recipe documents three.

## Code changes

- **Startup warning.** `RlsTransactionInterceptor` now logs a one-time `Logger.warn` on its first instantiation in a module load, flagging the trade-off and pointing at the new recipe. Class-level flag ensures subsequent instantiations in the same module load don't re-log. Pass `silentStartupWarning: true` once you've audited the choice.
- **New option.** `RlsTransactionOptions` gains `silentStartupWarning?: boolean`. Pass it via the `MTC_RLS_OPTIONS` provider.
- **Three new tests** pin the warning behavior: fires once, doesn't re-fire, suppressed by the flag.

## Docs changes

- **New section in `docs/advanced/recipes.md`**: "Auto-setting the RLS session variable" — covers all three strategies (interceptor; TypeORM subscriber + AsyncLocalStorage; scoped transactions inside services), the PgBouncer caveat for each, and a brief explainer on `set_config` vs `SET LOCAL`.
- **`docs/integration/rls-postgres.md`**: deleted the "Auto-set with `RlsTransactionInterceptor`" and "Performance considerations" sections. Replaced with a 3-strategy summary linking to the recipe.
- **`docs/advanced/security-best-practices.md`**: checklist item changed from `"RlsTransactionInterceptor is registered"` to `"One of the three RLS session-variable strategies is wired"`. Also updated two references to `validateRulesAtBuild` → `builder.validateRules` (renamed in 0.5.0-alpha but the doc had drifted).

## Drive-by fix: docs sidebar version drift

`docs/components/Layout.tsx` hardcoded the version as `v0.2.0-alpha`. That had drifted four releases without anyone noticing. Now sourced via `import libraryPkg from '../../package.json'` and rendered as `v{libraryPkg.version}`. Next.js inlines JSON at build time so this is zero-runtime-cost and drift-proof — every release moves the sidebar header automatically.

## Test plan

- [x] Library: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test:coverage && pnpm build` — green, **385 passed** (was 382), **100% coverage** holds.
- [x] Docs: `pnpm typecheck && DOCS_STATIC_EXPORT=true pnpm build` — green, 32 pages.
- [x] Example E2E: `pnpm sync:example:fast && pnpm test:e2e` — **60 passed | 4 skipped (64 total)**.
- [x] `/audit-cleanliness` clean.

## Version

`0.5.1-alpha` → `0.5.2-alpha`. Patch — no breaking API changes; the interceptor's behaviour is unchanged beyond the new warning, and the warning is suppressible.

## Backlog tracker

Item #7 in the 0.3.x → 0.5.x cycle plan. **One small item left:**

- **PR 8 — Theme 9H — housekeeping.** Delete the empty `test/integration/` and `test/e2e/` directories at the repo root. 15 minutes. Bumps `0.5.3-alpha`.

After that the cycle is closed and we can plan the next batch (Theme 7 PR E adversarial JWT scenarios, Theme 7 PRs B/C/D from the security-hardening test plan, or v1.0 production-soak preparation depending on priority).

## Summary
Closes #216. Replaces the `# TODO: Implement new statistics endpoint using ApplicationReview + ApplicationReviewItem` placeholder at `backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/college_review/utilities.py:37` with a working `GET /api/v1/college-review/statistics`.

## Shape
```jsonc
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "查詢成功",
  "data": {
    "per_scholarship": [
      {
        "scholarship_type_id": 1,
        "code": "phd",
        "name": "...",
        "name_en": "...",
        "applications": 2,
        "reviews_by_recommendation": { "approve": 1, "reject": 1 },
        "items_by_sub_type_and_recommendation": {
          "nstc": { "approve": 1, "reject": 1 },
          "moe_1w": { "reject": 1 }
        }
      }
    ],
    "totals": {
      "applications": 3,
      "reviews": 3,
      "reviews_by_recommendation": { "approve": 1, "partial_approve": 1, "reject": 1 },
      "items_by_recommendation": { "approve": 2, "reject": 2 }
    }
  }
}
```

## Design notes
- **No scoring**: per CLAUDE.md §7, the unified review system stores `recommendation` strings, not scores. The endpoint aggregates counts only.
- **Permission-scoped**: only `AdminScholarship` rows visible to the caller appear in `per_scholarship`. Users with no permissions get an empty payload (`success=true`), not a 403 — matches the rest of the college-review endpoints' behavior.
- **Four GROUP BY queries**: applications-per-type, reviews-by-recommendation, items-by-sub-type-recommendation, scholarship-name lookup. No N+1.
- **ApiResponse shape** (`{success, message, data}`) per CLAUDE.md §5.

## Summary

Implements the recognition engine described in spec PR #115:

- **Identity signature** (`get_identity_signature`): five-tuple of `(sleeve_uid, height_override, build_override, keyword_override, essential_item_type_ids)`. Essential-item slot is empty until PR-C.
- **Apparent UID** (`get_apparent_uid`): deterministic 16-char `blake2b` digest of the signature; returns `None` for pre-chargen shells. Two impostors with identical disguises still produce distinct UIDs because the real `sleeve_uid` is part of the signature.
- **Apparent gender** (`get_apparent_gender`): keyword override → catalog reverse-lookup → real grammar gender. Custom `@shortdesc` keywords always render neutral. Pronouns now follow the disguise everywhere they're rendered (`world/emote.py`, `commands/CmdInventory.py` frisk path).
- **Recognition re-keying**: `recognition_memory` is keyed on Apparent UID instead of real `sleeve_uid` everywhere — `get_display_name`, `world/search` assigned-name match, and the full `remember`/`forget`/`recall`/`memory` cluster. A character under disguise produces a distinct entry from their real form.
- **`lost_contact` field**: added to memory entries, surfaced in `recall` and `memory` output as `(lost contact)`. The periodic prune job that flips this flag is deferred — the engine PR adds the field + render only.
- **Idempotent legacy wipe**: `wipe_all_legacy_recognition_memory` runs on `at_server_start` and removes any entry whose key length ≠ 16 or whose value lacks `lost_contact`. Becomes a no-op once migrated; carries a TODO to be removed after deployment is verified clean.

- `apparent_uid_for(char)` — derives the UID for a mock character

Six identity-adjacent test modules migrated to use it. New tests in `test_identity.py` cover: signature shape, UID determinism, sleeve-salt distinctness, gender derivation across all override paths, and wipe migration idempotency.

body:
## Summary

Throttles shell tool text `data` events to `OUTPUT_UPDATE_INTERVAL_MS` (1s), matching
the existing `binary_progress` cadence, and caps the live UI buffer to
`LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` (100k chars). Without throttling, every chunk
triggered a full React re-render of the shell output panel; commands emitting
thousands of lines (build warnings, manifest generation, verbose test runs)
pinned the UI until the command exited.

## Details

This PR builds on the feedback @jacob314 left on the previous attempt (#25461)
and resolves the three concerns raised there:

1. **No initial 1s delay** — `lastUpdateTime` starts at `0` and the first text
   chunk renders immediately. Subsequent chunks are throttled.
2. **Bounded live buffer** — the new `appendToLiveOutputBuffer` keeps only the
   last `LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BUFFER_CHARS` characters for the live preview, removing
   the unbounded-string growth risk. The complete output is unaffected: it is
   still rendered from the full result returned by `shellExecutionService` after
   the command exits.
3. **PTY snapshots not throttled** — `AnsiOutput` (PTY mode) chunks bypass the
   throttle entirely, preserving responsiveness for progress bars and
   curses-style UIs.

Final-state guarantee: `flushOutput()` runs on the `exit` event and again after
`resultPromise` resolves (non-background path), so the last frame is always
flushed without delay.

## Related Issues

Fixes #25459

Supersedes #22843 (closed under the help-wanted policy) and #25461 (closed for
inactivity after change requests).

## How to Validate

1. Build the bundle: `npm run bundle`
2. Run a high-volume shell command from inside the CLI:
   `for i in $(seq 1 20000); do echo "line $i"; done`
3. Verify the UI stays responsive while the command runs (no freeze, input
   stays interactive) and the final output is complete and correct.
4. Run a PTY-style command (e.g. anything that emits ANSI progress) and verify
   updates still appear at full rate (no throttle on PTY).
5. Run the regression tests:
   `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/tools/shell.test.ts`

## Summary

Headline perf gain identified by the performance-engineer in the joint cryptanalysis perf consult. The batch GCD's product/remainder tree is >97% of total cryptanalysis wall time; libgmp's FFT-based bignum multiplication is dramatically faster than CPython int's Karatsuba on the operand sizes involved (~25 MB root product at 100k keys).

## Measured speedups (in profiler)

| Fleet size | Pure Python (Karatsuba) | gmpy2 (libgmp FFT) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 500 keys | 2.81 s | 0.076 s | **37×** |
| 1,000 keys | 10.93 s | 0.187 s | **59×** |
| 2,000 keys | 42.90 s | 0.485 s | **88×** |
| 100,000 keys (extrap) | ~25 hours | ~100 seconds | **~900×** |

## Implementation

- Module-level `_HAS_GMPY2` detection at the top of `certparse/reports/cryptanalysis.py`.
- `_batch_gcd` wraps inbound moduli with `gmpy2.mpz` and uses `gmpy2.gcd` when available; falls back to CPython `int` + `math.gcd` otherwise.
- `_build_product_tree` and `_remainder_tree` are representation-agnostic — Python operator overloading dispatches `mpz.__mul__` / `mpz.__mod__` automatically.
- Factor values cast back to `int` before returning so `Report.detail` stays JSON-clean.
- `Report.attributes.batch_gcd_backend` reports `'gmpy2'` or `'stdlib'`.

## Dependency change

- New optional extras: `pip install certparse[fast]` brings in `gmpy2>=2.1`.
- Added to `dev` extras too so CI exercises the gmpy2 path (parity test).
- Stdlib path remains the unconditional fallback.

body:
## Summary

- Closes [CTL-334](https://linear.app/coalesce-labs/issue/CTL-334)
- `orchestrate-dispatch-next` was leaking the parent shell's herestring stdin into backgrounded `claude -p` worker subshells, causing the first worker(s) in a multi-row dispatch to receive leftover `<wave>\t<ticket>` lines as prompt input and exit with launch-failure
- Two confirmed repros on the ticket — original (`hud-fixes-2026-05-11`, CTL-332) and 2026-05-12 (`orch-adv-912-2026-05-12`, ADV-916)
- Adds a regression test that fails with the bug present (only 1 of 3 dispatched, leaked stdin observable) and passes with the fix

## Root cause

The dispatch loop iterates over PENDING via `while IFS=$'\t' read -r W T; do ... done <<< "$PENDING"`. Inside the loop, the launch site is:

```bash
(
  cd "$WORKER_DIR" || exit 1
  ...
  exec nohup "$CLAUDE_BIN" ... -p "..."
) > "$STREAM" 2> "$STDERR" &
```

The backgrounded subshell inherits stdin from the parent — the herestring that `read` is draining one line at a time. `claude -p` reads stdin even in non-interactive mode and treats the leftover TSV rows as additional prompt input. The first AskUserQuestion in the worker (asking what the trailing `<wave>\t<ticket>` token means) errors out in headless `-p` mode and the worker exits as launch-failure within seconds.

## Fix

Add `</dev/null` on the launch subshell so claude can't inherit the parent's stdin. `orchestrate-revive` already does this at line 225 — the new code matches that pattern.

Files changed:

| File | What | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| `plugins/dev/scripts/orchestrate-dispatch-next` | `</dev/null` on launch subshell + explanatory comment | Primary fix |
| `plugins/dev/templates/dispatch-fixup.sh.template` | `</dev/null` on launch subshell | Defense-in-depth: future change can't regress the pattern |
| `plugins/dev/templates/dispatch-rebase.sh.template` | `</dev/null` on launch subshell | Same |
| `plugins/dev/scripts/orchestrate-followup` | `</dev/null` on the printed launch command template | Same |
| `plugins/dev/scripts/__tests__/orchestrate-dispatch-next.test.sh` | New test 23 (CTL-334) | Regression coverage |

The regression test redefines the fake `claude` binary to drain stdin into a per-PID file, then dispatches 3 tickets and asserts (a) all 3 are dispatched in a single call and (b) every per-worker stdin capture is empty. Verified by stashing the fix and re-running: test 23 fails with `got: T-1 (stdin leak symptom: only first N-1 dispatched)` and `LEAK ... 1\tT-2\n1\tT-3` — matches the exact symptom from the ticket repros.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash plugins/dev/scripts/__tests__/orchestrate-fixup.test.sh` — 21 pass

body:
## Summary

Adds the framed counterparts of the existing `L2capChannel.incoming(decoder)` / `L2capChannel.write(value, encoder)` codec extensions:

- `L2capChannel.framedIncoming(decoder, framer, onDecodeFailure): Flow<T>`
- `L2capChannel.writeFramed(value, encoder, framer)`

Both default to `LengthPrefixFramer()`. Pure composition over the existing `decodeFramed` operator and `Framer.frame` primitive - no new state, no platform code.

## Motivation

The existing pair handles the 1-packet = 1-message case. Streaming workloads (telemetry, batched sensor events, structured payloads larger than a single L2CAP packet) need framing so the receiver can reassemble logical messages independently of how the transport delivers chunks. Today callers reach for `channel.incoming.decodeFramed(decoder, framer, onDecodeFailure)` manually; `framedIncoming` is a 1-line wrapper that keeps the call site readable.

## Behavior

- Decoder failures on a frame route to `onDecodeFailure` and are dropped; remaining frames continue.
- `FrameTooLargeException` (malformed length prefix) terminates the flow; consumers recover via `.catch { }`.
- Partial frames spanning packet boundaries are buffered transparently by the underlying `Unframer`.

## Tests

7 new cases in `L2capCodecTest.kt` (11/11 pass on jvmTest):

- `writeFramedPrefixesLengthHeader` - asserts the 4-byte LE length prefix.
- `framedIncomingDecodesMultiFrameStream` - 3 framed packets in, 3 typed values out.
- `framedIncomingRoutesDecodeFailureToCallback` - bad payload between two good ones, callback fires, stream continues.
- `framedIncomingPropagatesFrameTooLargeException` - oversize length prefix, caught via `.catch`.
- `writeFramedRoundTripsThroughFramedIncoming` - sender writes 3 values, receiver decodes 3 values.
- `framedIncomingHandlesPacketBoundariesDifferentFromFrameBoundaries` - frame split across two packets, decoded as one.
- `writeFramedAndFramedIncomingDefaultToLengthPrefixFramer` - default-framer round trip + header present.

## Verify

- `:kmp-ble-codec:jvmTest` 11/11 pass
- `:kmp-ble-codec:compileKotlinIosSimulatorArm64` clean
- `:kmp-ble-codec:compileAndroidMain` clean

body:
## Summary

Remove the PreBuildEvent that copies Bootstrap build artifacts from a gitignored `dist` folder on every build, and add a convenience script for rebuilding Bootstrap from LESS sources.

## Problem

The `NuGetGallery.csproj` PreBuildEvent copied `bootstrap.min.css` and `bootstrap.js` from `src/Bootstrap/dist/` into the gallery project on every build. The `dist` folder is gitignored and only populated by running `grunt` locally. If the `dist` files were stale (built from older LESS sources), the copy overwrote the committed files with outdated content, producing a phantom diff that had to be manually discarded when staging changes.

## Changes

1. **Removed the PreBuildEvent** from `NuGetGallery.csproj` that copied from the gitignored `dist` folder.
2. **Removed tracked files from `src/Bootstrap/dist/`** (`bootstrap.css`, `bootstrap-theme.css`, `bootstrap.js`) since they are build artifacts. Updated `.gitignore` to ignore the entire `dist` directory. The committed copies in the gallery project are the source of truth.
3. **Added `tools/Build-Bootstrap.ps1`** as a convenience script for rebuilding Bootstrap from LESS sources. It runs `npm install` (if needed) and `grunt`, which compiles, minifies, and copies the output to the gallery project.
4. **Updated `src/Bootstrap/README.md`** with instructions for rebuilding after modifying LESS files.

## Testing

- Verified `git status` is clean after build and deploy with no changes.
- Verified that modifying a LESS variable, running `Build-Bootstrap.ps1`, and committing produces the expected changes in both the LESS source and the gallery CSS output.
- Verified that deploying after committing produces no phantom diffs.

# Implementación de Circuit Breaker con Resilience4j

Esta solicitud de extracción introduce soporte para **Circuit Breaker** utilizando **Resilience4j** en los servicios de autenticación (`AuthService`) e inventario (`InventarioService`). Estos cambios mejoran la resiliencia de la aplicación ante posibles fallos en los microservicios downstream, permitiendo un manejo elegante de errores y mayor estabilidad del sistema.

## Integración de Resiliencia y Circuit Breaker

* **Anotaciones de Resilience4j**: Se añadieron anotaciones `@CircuitBreaker` a todos los métodos en `AuthService` e `InventarioService`. Se especificaron métodos de *fallback* para gestionar fallos y mejorar la robustez del sistema.
* **Métodos de Fallback**: Se implementaron métodos de respaldo en ambos servicios que lanzan una `ResponseStatusException` con estado `503 Service Unavailable` cuando los servicios dependientes no están disponibles, centralizando así el manejo de errores de conectividad.

## Actualizaciones de Dependencias y Configuración

* **`pom.xml`**: Se añadió la dependencia `resilience4j-spring-boot3` para dar soporte al Circuit Breaker.
* **Configuración**: Se incluyeron los ajustes específicos de Resilience4j para las instancias de `authService` e `inventoryService` en el archivo `application.properties`.
* **Ajuste de Versión**: Se realizó un downgrade de la versión del parent de Spring Boot de `4.0.6` a `4.0.0` para cumplir con requisitos de compatibilidad.

## Documentación y Correcciones Menores

* Se corrigieron errores tipográficos y se mejoraron los comentarios en `AuthController.java` y `application.properties` para mayor claridad del código.

---
Con estos cambios, el sistema ahora es capaz de detectar fallos en cascada y proteger la disponibilidad de la plataforma mediante mecanismos de autoprotección.

body:
### 💡 What
Refactored `SmartFailover.executeBatch()` to replace `array.map()` and `Promise.allSettled()` with a native async worker pool utilizing `Array.from()` and `Promise.all()`. Additionally, modified the object cloning behavior inside hot loops to use `Object.assign({}, options)` instead of object spreading `{...options}` or `Object.create(options)`.

### 🎯 Why
In large batch request scenarios, mapping over large arrays with `Promise.allSettled` creates significant heap allocation overhead from intermediate array generation and upfront closure allocations per item. The previous fallback serial implementation also used `Object.create(options)` which unsafely attached properties to the prototype chain instead of producing own properties, risking subtle downstream bugs where object iteration expects safe properties.

### 📊 Impact
* **Memory footprint reduction:** Eliminates the upfront instantiation of intermediate closure promises and spread iterators during iteration. 
* **Safe execution:** Ensures options are consistently deeply copied as "own properties" (`Object.assign`) without prototype pollution.
* **Latency reduction:** Async worker pools with dynamically populated pre-allocated arrays (`results.length = len`) skip the array resizing overhead of `array.push()`.

### 🔬 Measurement
Run `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 npx vitest run __tests__/unit/services/SmartFailover.test.js` to verify exact behavioral equivalence (preserves `index` mapping correctly, handles mixed rejections/resolutions identically, and preserves original `this` context binding).

base is #151) — review/merge in order: #151 → #152 → this. Closes the
loop on the user's original ask: an actual bracket UI, one-dimension-per-
session workflow, and the "first task repeats forever" anchor problem
finally gone (via PR 2's `selectNextPair`).

## Summary

**New: `TournamentBracket.tsx`**
- ReactFlow visualization. Columns by loss count: winners' bracket on the
  left, items with N losses on column N. Items within a column sorted by
  win count.
- Direct (non-transitive) wins shown as edges to avoid clutter.
- Active matchup: orange outline. Placed items (final rank fully
  determined): green outline + rank label.
- Pan/zoom/drag disabled — read-only embed inside the modal.

**TaskSlideshow refactor**
- Single-dimension mode: a Radio.Group in the header switches between
  Importance and Urgency. Only the active dimension is asked per pair.
- Auto-default on first open: pick whichever dimension has more
  unresolved pairs.
- `selectNextPair()` from PR 2 picks one matchup at a time; `recentItems`
  window of 6 enforces anti-anchor so the same task can't dominate.
- Soft completion: when a dimension finishes, you land on a screen that
  offers "Continue with [other dimension]" or "Apply Rankings" — you can
  ship partial rankings.
- Progress tag in header: `12/45 pairs · 27%`.
- Removed: prev/next buttons, the priority→urgency auto-advance, the
  dual-minimap render, the Fisher-Yates shuffle helper, and ~6 dead
  state variables.

**Cleanup**
- Deleted `ComparisonGraphMinimap.tsx` (orphaned).
- Dropped unused `IconLeft`/`IconRight` imports.

## Test plan

I can't run the UI here, so the manual smoke needs to happen on your machine:

- [ ] Open the slideshow with ≥4 items. Confirm the bracket renders and
      the current matchup is highlighted in orange.
- [ ] Answer 5–6 pairs. Confirm the same task does NOT anchor every match
      (the anti-anchor heuristic should rotate items).
- [ ] Switch dimensions mid-session. Confirm the bracket re-renders for
      the new dimension and selectNextPair picks a sensible matchup.
- [ ] Close and re-open the modal. Confirm progress survives (PR 1
      persistence still works alongside the new UI).
- [ ] Add a new task while the slideshow is closed, then reopen. Confirm
      the new task appears and the algorithm prioritizes pairs involving
      it (PR 2's insertNewItem isn't wired in yet — but selectNextPair

- [ ] Click "Apply Rankings" mid-session. Confirm importance/urgency get
      written to tasks/workflows in the database.
- [ ] "Start Over" should clear DB rows for both dimensions and reset the
      bracket.

## What's NOT in this PR

- `insertNewItem()` (from PR 2) isn't wired into the UI explicitly —
  `selectNextPair` handles new items through its info-gain heuristic. We
  can add an explicit "insert mode" later if the user wants more
  aggressive binary-search behavior.
- Keyboard shortcuts for switching dimensions (only `1` / `2` / `=` /

Adds Apple Silicon (MLX) backend for the Gemma 4 31B-IT model. The same quantized checkpoint works for both CUDA and MLX — backend-specific packing happens at load time.

Key changes:

- MLX packer converts Int4Tensor → IntxUnpackedToInt8Tensor for MLX's quantized linear fusion
- Source transforms replace PyTorch ops with mlx.rope, mlx.kv_cache_update, mlx.custom_sdpa for optimized Metal kernels
- Proportional partial RoPE (full-attention layers) passes 1D frequencies to mlx.rope with dims=rotary_dim, fixing the C++ runtime to pass base=nullopt when freqs is provided
- Single-method export with dynamic seq_len and host-side sampling
- C++ runner supports both backends via #ifdef, using shared logits_to_token for MLX sampling
- Last-logits-only optimization: lm_head always runs on last position only, removing the full-logits codepath entirely

The backend `nest build` fails with 34 TypeScript errors. body:
## Summary
- New `maw self-update` plugin at `src/commands/plugins/self-update/` — pulls origin into the local bun-linked maw-js checkout, re-binds via `bun link`. Distinct from `maw update` (which reinstalls a published ref globally).
- Flags: `--dry-run`, `--check`, `--branch=<NAME>` (default `alpha`), `--force` (auto-stash + restore around pull).
- `maw --version` appends `⚠ local is N commits behind origin/<branch> — run \`maw self-update\`` when `.git/FETCH_HEAD` is fresh (<1 h) and the branch is actually behind — cheap heuristic, no extra fetches per `--version` call.

## Behavior
- Refuses dirty checkout (suggests `--force`), detached HEAD, branch mismatch (suggests `git checkout <target>` or `--branch=<current>`).
- Pulls `--ff-only` only — never auto-merges. Surfaces the underlying git error if the pull isn't a fast-forward.
- Runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` only when `bun.lock` / `bun.lockb` / `package.json` changed in the pulled range (non-fatal warning if it fails).
- Reports before/after short SHAs + commit subjects (capped at 12; "... and N more" tail for larger pulls).
- `--force` + dirty: stash → pull → stash pop, with restore on pull failure.

## Implementation notes
- `impl.ts` accepts an injected `Runner` (`exec(cmd, args, opts)` → `{ code, stdout, stderr }`). Default runner uses `spawnSync`; tests inject a scripted fake — no real shell-outs in CI.
- Checkout resolution: `resolve(import.meta.dir, "../../../..")` walks four levels up from `src/commands/plugins/self-update/impl.ts` to the repo root.
- Worktree-aware in `cmd-version.ts`: uses `git rev-parse --git-dir` instead of joining `.git/FETCH_HEAD` (worktrees have `.git` as a file).

## Test plan
- [x] `MAW_TEST_MODE=1 bun test test/plugins/self-update.test.ts` — 16 pass / 0 fail (66 expect calls), covering: synced, behind, dirty refusal, `--force` stash flow, pull-fails + stash restore, `--check` (synced + behind), `--dry-run`, `--branch`, branch-mismatch, detached HEAD, missing `.git`, handler dispatch.
- [x] `MAW_TEST_MODE=1 bun test test/plugins/` — 40 pass / 0 fail (combined with pane tests).
- [x] `MAW_TEST_MODE=1 bun test test/plugins-cli.test.ts test/plugins.test.ts` — 43 pass / 0 fail (existing plugin tests unaffected).
- [x] Smoke: `bun src/cli.ts --version` still prints the version line cleanly (warning empty for this fresh worktree branch).
- [x] Smoke: `maw self-update --help` returns full usage.

## Out of scope
- No `package.json` bump — release is a separate gesture (`/release-alpha`).
- CONTRIBUTING.md doc update (acceptance criterion in #1271) — left for a follow-up doc-only PR.

body:
## Summary

This PR has grown well past the original \"OEM auth design docs\" scope. It's the full **cloud-v2 bootstrap**: monorepo, design docs, working implementation for the first two services, and the AWS infra to run them.

### Design docs (`cloud-v2/docs/issues/`)
- **001-oem-auth** — OEM authentication via OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693). Locked on Option 5 (JWT bearer + exchange) after considering SAML/OIDC SSO, code flow, direct-bearer, S2S API. OEM-attested installation JWTs → Mentra access/refresh pair.
- **002-oem-portal** — OEM admin portal spike (scope only; not built).
- **003-audio** — Stateless, failover-ready audio path with **dual ingress (UDP + WS)** using the v1 packet format. Ownership in Redis, workers do LC3 decode + provider call.

### Monorepo (`cloud-v2/`)
- Bun workspaces: `@mentra/cloud-{core,audio,proxy,shared}`. TS project refs, runnable stubs.
- `scripts/setup.ts` preflight (Bun/Docker/Redis idempotent boot).
- `@mentra/cloud-shared`: `pino` logger w/ pod/env metadata, `/healthz` + `/ready` (hono).

### Core (`packages/core`)
- **OEM OAuth**: token-exchange grant (`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`). Installation-attested JWTs in, Mentra access+refresh tokens out. Signed with Ed25519 keys from `MENTRA_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY` / `MENTRA_JWT_PUBLIC_KEY`.
- **Sessions** in Mongo, **bearer middleware** verifies tokens on every API call.
- Mongo + Redis connections plug into `/ready`.

### Audio (`packages/audio`)
- **UDP ingress** on `:8000` (NLB-fronted in AWS).
- **Ownership service** routes packets to the owning pod via Redis — any pod can ingress, the right pod processes.
- **Worker pool**: dedicated workers do LC3 decode (`liblc3.wasm`) + STT provider call. Providers: `soniox` (real) and `mock` (tests). `AUDIO_PROVIDER` selects.

### AWS infra (us-west-2)
- **Porter** app (`porter.yaml`) builds one image, runs core + audio + proxy services with per-service `run:` overrides.
- **Dockerfile** pinned to `oven/bun:1.3.14` — Bun ≤1.2.x had a `node:tls` polyfill bug that broke MongoDB Atlas SNI (`Right side of assignment cannot be destructured at checkServerIdentity`).
- **UDP NLB** (`deploy/audio-udp-nlb.yaml`) — separate k8s Service because Porter's `additionalPorts:` exposes the container port but doesn't provision an AWS NLB. Critical bit: `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` so k8s allocates a TCP `healthCheckNodePort` the AWS LB Controller picks up automatically (NLB target groups can only TCP-healthcheck even for UDP listeners).
- **Doppler** (`doppler.yaml`, project `cloud-v2`, configs `dev`/`dev_aws`/`staging`/`prod`) integrated with Porter env groups; ~5s propagation on secret changes.
- **MongoDB Atlas** (project `Cloud2`, cluster `dev`) for state.
- **ElastiCache** (`cloud-elasticache-us-west-2`, TLS, `rediss://`) for ownership + pubsub.
- **Soniox** as the production STT provider.

### Runbooks (`cloud-v2/docs/runbooks/`)
Written for engineers joining the team — \"what is this, why is it this way, where does it live\" — not first-time-setup tutorials:
- `infra.md`, `aws.md`, `porter/deploys.md`, `doppler/porter-integration.md`
- `cloudflare/dns-for-nlb.md`, `deploy/udp-nlb-aws.md`
- `conventions/naming.md`, `incident-response/pod-crash-loop.md`

### Tests (`tests/`, `test/test-{oem,client}`)
- `audio.integration` — full UDP pipeline with mock provider.
- `audio.multipod.integration` — cross-pod ownership handoff via Redis.
- `audio.soak.integration` — 60s soak to catch leaks.
- `oem-auth.integration` — OEM grant happy path + failure modes.
- `lc3.decoder.test` — wasm decoder sanity.
- `scripts/soniox-smoke.ts` — in-process e2e against the **real Soniox API** (boots core + audio + test-oem, sends real LC3 audio, asserts a transcript).

### Out of scope (follow-ups)
- Proxy service (`@mentra/cloud-proxy`) — stubs only, no impl yet.
- Prod Atlas cluster + prod Porter target.
- Cross-region Atlas read-only replicas (us-east-2, EU) for prod regional deploys — tickets to be filed.
- Cloudflare DNS for the audio NLB (runbook documents the steps; not yet applied).

## Test plan

- [x] Local e2e: TestClient → core (token exchange) → audio (UDP) → Soniox → transcript (`bun run scripts/soniox-smoke.ts`)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean (gate in Dockerfile)
- [x] `bun test` (integration suites, mock provider)
- [x] Deployed to AWS us-west-2 (`aws-us-west-2` EKS, Porter project)
- [x] UDP NLB provisioned and target group healthy (`externalTrafficPolicy: Local`)
- [x] Doppler ↔ Porter sync verified (<5s propagation on secret change)
- [x] Atlas allowlist opened for EKS NAT egress IP; core pod connects to Mongo
- [ ] Full deployed e2e: TestClient → deployed NLB → audio pod → Soniox → transcript
- [ ] Cloudflare DNS pointed at the NLB (DNS-only, no orange-cloud — UDP would blackhole)

> **High Risk**
> Greenfield but touches authentication, session tokens, Mongo/Redis coordination, and production-facing UDP/NLB wiring—bugs or misconfig could break login, transcripts, or cross-pod audio ownership.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`cloud-v2/`** as a new horizontally scalable cloud stack for the local miniapp SDK: Bun workspaces (`@mentra/cloud-core`, `@mentra/cloud-runtime`, `@mentra/cloud-proxy`, `@mentra/cloud-shared`, `@mentra/cloud-client`), dev/test Docker compose, setup scripts, and a shared Dockerfile that typechecks on build.
> 
> **Cloud core** implements RFC 8693 **token exchange** and rotating refresh (`/api/client/auth/exchange`, `/refresh`), **miniapp-scoped tokens**, **JWKS**, Mongo-backed OEM/user/session state, and Ed25519 signing—documented end-to-end under `docs/issues/001-cloud-core/auth/`.
> 
> **Cloud runtime** (audio + camera) follows the specced model: stateless **UDP/WS ingress**, Redis stream routing, per-user **ownership** with TTL failover, **worker pool** for LC3 decode and STT providers (Soniox/mock), subscription REST, and camera managed-photo/stream APIs. Large architecture and fault-regression docs live under `docs/issues/002-cloud-runtime/`.
> 
> **Deploy & ops**: Porter manifests for core/runtime/mongo/redis, **UDP NLB** Service for audio ingress (`externalTrafficPolicy: Local`), `.dockerignore`/`.gitignore` for the tree, and repo root gitignore exceptions for `cloud-v2/docs/issues/`.
> 
> **Tests & harness**: `test-oem` fixture, integration/soak tests, and an audio fault E2E script for phone QA. Proxy remains stubbed; several auth/miniapp/console services are doc placeholders for later work.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/hilarious-tapioca-625b16/agent-runs/6a039ee2fe8491ba61281ff0

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** Kok gak bisa di deploy?

✅ **Result:** # Deployment Fixes

Two issues were preventing the site from deploying and working correctly on Netlify.

## Missing `netlify.toml`

The project had no Netlify configuration file. Without it, Netlify relies entirely on auto-detection to figure out how to build and serve a Next.js app. For a Next.js 16 project — which introduces a new Adapter API and breaking changes from earlier versions — auto-detection is not reliable. A `netlify.toml` was added that explicitly declares the build command (`npm run build`), the output directory (`.next`), and the `@netlify/plugin-nextjs` plugin. The plugin is what enables Netlify to correctly handle Next.js App Router features such as Server Components, Route Handlers, and image optimization.

## `/api/upscale` Function Timeout

The upscale API route polled an external image processing service in a server-side loop with 30 iterations at 2.5-second intervals, meaning a single request could keep a serverless function running for up to 75 seconds. Netlify serverless functions have a hard execution limit (26 seconds on paid plans, 10 seconds on the free tier), so this endpoint would always time out in production, causing every upscale request to return a 504 error.

The polling loop was reduced to 8 iterations at 2-second intervals (≈16 seconds max polling time), and `export const maxDuration = 25` was added to the route file so Next.js and Netlify both know to allocate the full 25-second window for this endpoint. Upload time plus polling now comfortably fits within that budget.

## Summary of files changed

- **`netlify.toml`** — created; declares build command, publish directory, and the `@netlify/plugin-nextjs` plugin.
- **`app/api/upscale/route.js`** — reduced polling loop from 30 × 2500ms to 8 × 2000ms and added `export const maxDuration = 25`.

body:
## Summary

- **Fixes #621** — `langstripstructuremarkers` was over-stripping trailing `}` when the line contained an inline one-line nested block (e.g. `try {body}}`). The strip removed both closing braces, leaving the inline `{` unmatched in stored node text. The outline-export pass couldn't reconstruct the missing `}` because the inline block doesn't correspond to an outline level transition. Result: one `}` lost per occurrence, breaking compile.
- **Reinstalls `databases/Virgin.root`'s `system.startup.startupScript`** from its `.ut` file, fixing a pre-existing corruption (line-3 compile error at REPL boot) that motivated the entire #616/#618/#586/#621 chain.

## Root cause

`langstripstructuremarkers` strips trailing `{`/`}`/`;`/whitespace from non-comment lines because the outline-export pass (`oplangtextvisit`) re-derives structural markers from outline level transitions. The 5 round-trip tests added in #616 covered shallow nesting and didn't catch the case where a single source line both opens AND closes an inline block.

Concrete example from `system/startup/startupScript.ut` line 221:

```usertalk
if system.environment.isMac {
    try {new (tableType, @user.odbEditors.data.openFiles)}}; //comment
```

The trailing `}};` closes both the inline `try` and the parent `if`. Naive backward-strip removed all three characters, storing `try {new (...)` with an unmatched `{`. The outline-export pass re-emits `}` at level transitions, but this line stays at one level (its body is inline, not a child node), so the second `}` was never reconstructed. Result on the 241-line startup script: 83 `{` but only 82 `}` — script no longer compiles, line-242 syntax error at REPL boot.

## Fix

When stripping a trailing `}`, balance-count the kept content. If removing this `}` would leave surplus opens, stop. The check respects string-literal state (both `"..."` and `«...»` smart-quote forms with `\`-escapes), so braces inside strings don't confuse the count.

For `try {new (...)}};`:
- Strip `;` (not a brace; pass)
- Try to strip last `}`: kept content `try {new (...)}` has opens=1, closes=1 → balanced → strip OK
- Try to strip next `}`: kept content `try {new (...)` would have opens=1, closes=0 → surplus opens → STOP

Result stored: `try {new (...)}` (matched brace pair preserved). Export adds the outer `}` from the level transition.

## Test plan

- [x] `./tools/run_headless_tests.sh` — 489 / 489 unit pass
- [x] `cd tests && make test-integration` — 2013 pass / 296 skipped / 0 failed
- [x] New round-trip tests at depth 1 and outermost depth — both pass
- [x] Verified RED baseline: stashed the fix, rebuilt, ran the new test → FAIL. Restored fix → PASS
- [x] Local `/gate` bar-raiser review — PASS, two P2 cleanups applied (commit 2)
- [x] Manual probe on real startupScript: balanced 83 `{` / 83 `}` after round-trip (was 83 / 82 before)
- [x] REPL boot on reinstalled `databases/Virgin.root`: no `lang-ERROR` lines (was "line 3: syntax error" on develop)

## Note on Virgin.root binary size

`databases/Virgin.root` grew from 16.9 MB to 20.6 MB (+22%) after the reinstall. Expected — this is reinstalling `system.startup.startupScript` (a real ~11KB script) on top of the existing corrupted form, plus normal ODB-save metadata. Not binary corruption or debug-symbol inclusion; just normal content growth.

## Closes

- Issue #621 (round-trip brace drop)
- Task #105 in the agent task list (startupScript reinstall — was blocked on this)
